chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a contracted slave-woman who had paid two-thirds of her contract, and it had been stipulated upon her that if she became unable (to pay the remainder), she would be returned to slavery, and we would be released from what we had taken from her, and two installments had accumulated upon her.
He (peace be upon him) said: She is returned (to slavery), and it pleases them (is accepted) what they took from her.
And he (peace be upon him) said: It is not for her to delay the installment after its due date for one month, except with their permission.

key_terms.مُكَاتَبَةٍ: Contract of manumission where a slave pays a fixed sum for freedom

ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave's payment if she defaults on her final installment in a mukatabah contract?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial and legal consequences when a mukataba (slave seeking manumission) defaults on the final third of her contract, ruling that she reverts to slavery while the master retains the paid portion. The narration further establishes a protective procedural rule: the master cannot unilaterally postpone an installment deadline by more than one month without the slave's consent, ensuring fairness in the contractual timeline. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing the master's property rights with the slave's dignity and contractual stability.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a contracted woman who has paid off two-thirds of her contract, and it had been stipulated upon her that if she was frustrated (from paying), so she would be returned to the slavery, and we would be in the leeway from what we take from her, and two installments had gathered upon her.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would be returned, and make good for them what they take from her’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for her that she delays the installment after the passing by of one month except by their permission’.
